chantedPrayers.text: Liberating Prayer O Blessed One, Shakyamuni Buddha, precious Treasury of Compassion, Bestower of Supreme Inner Peace. You who love all beings without exception are the source of happiness and goodness, and you guide us to the liberating path. Your body is a wish-fulfilling jewel, your speech is supreme, purifying nectar, and your mind is refuge for all living beings. With folded palms I turn to you, Supreme unchanging Friend. I request from the depths of my heart, please give me the light of your wisdom to dispel the darkness of my mind and to heal my mental continuum. Please nourish me with your goodness, that I in turn may nourish all beings with an unceasing banquet of delight. Through your compassionate intention, your blessings and virtuous deeds, and my strong wish to rely upon you, may all suffering quickly cease and all happiness and joy be fulfilled, and may holy Dharma flourish forevermore. Going for Refuge I and all sentient beings, until we achieve enlightenment, go for refuge to Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. I and all sentient beings, until we achieve enlightenment, go for refuge to Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. I and all sentient beings, until we achieve enlightenment, go for refuge to Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. Generating Bodhichitta Through the virtues I collect by giving and other perfections, may I become a Buddha for the benefit of all. Through the virtues I collect by giving and other perfections, may I become a Buddha for the benefit of all. Through the virtues I collect by giving and other perfections, may I become a Buddha for the benefit of all. Four Immeasurables May everyone be happy, May everyone be free from misery, May no one ever be separated from their happiness, May everyone have equanimity, free from hatred and attachment. Visualizing the Field for Accumulating Merit In the space before me is the living Buddha Shakyamuni, surrounded by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, like the full moon surrounded by stars. Prayer of Seven Limbs With my body, speech, and mind, humbly I prostrate, and make offerings both set out and imagined. I confess my wrong deeds from all time and rejoice in the virtues of all. Please stay until samsara ceases and turn the Wheel of Dharma for us. I dedicate all virtues to great enlightenment. Offering the Mandala The ground sprinkled with perfume and spread with flowers, The Great Mountain, four lands, sun and moon, Seen as a Buddha Land and offered thus, May all beings enjoy such Pure Lands. The objects that give rise to my attachment, hatred, and confusion, my friends, enemies, and strangers, our bodies and enjoyments — please accept these and bless me to be released directly from the three poisons. IDAM GURU RATNA MANDALAKAM NIRYATAYAMI. Prayer of the Stages of the Path The path begins with strong reliance On my kind Teacher, source of all good; O Bless me with this understanding To follow him with great devotion. This human life with all its freedoms, Exceedingly rare and most meaningful — O Bless me with this understanding All day and night to seize its essence. My body, like a water bubble, Decays and dies so very quickly; After death come results of karma, Just as the shadow of a body. With this firm knowledge and target of remembrance Bless me to be extremely cautious, Always avoiding harmful actions And gathering abundant virtue. Samsara’s pleasures are deceptive, Give no contentment, only torment; So please bless me to strive sincerely To gain the bliss of perfect freedom. O Bless me so that from this pure thought Come great unfailing conscientiousness, To keep as my essential practice The Dharma’s root, the Pratimoksha. Just like myself, all my kind mothers Are drowning in samsara’s ocean; O So that I may soon release them, Bless me to train in bodhichitta. But I cannot become a Buddha By this alone without three ethics; So bless me with the strength to practise The Bodhisattva’s ordination. By pacifying my distractions And analyzing perfect meanings, Bless me to quickly gain the union Of special insight and quiescence. When I become a pure container Through the karma path, bless me to enter The essence practice of good fortune, The supreme vehicle, the Tantra. The two attainments both depend on My sacred vows and my commitments; Bless me to understand this clearly And keep them at the cost of my life. By constant practice in four sessions, The way explained by holy Teachers, O Bless me to gain both the stages Which are the essence of the Tantras. May those who guide me on the good path And my companions all have long lives; Bless me to pacify completely All obstacles, outer and inner. May I always find perfect Teachers And take delight in holy Dharma, Accomplish all grounds and paths swiftly, And gain the state of Vajradhara. Receiving Blessings From the hearts of all the holy beings, streams of light and nectar flow down, granting blessings and purifying.

postMeditation.speaker: Kadam Kyle
postMeditation.text:
Okay, let's see. Online there's Ben and Kristin, Grady, Dale. And then in person, Sumit, Mary Ann, Anne P, Neil, David, Jose, Ryan, Byron, Fran, Anne, Mimi, and Suzanne.

We were finishing up refuge last time. And so this is our last shot ever talking about refuge, so share what you got or didn't get. And then we're swiftly moving on to confession, purification practice, which is extremely thrilling.

practiceReports.speaker: Fran
practiceReports.text:
I've been continuing my focus on receiving blessings and asking for blessings. Mainly when I sit down to meditate, I've been starting by asking for blessings to concentrate on my meditation. And if I get distracted, I bring myself back with a request for blessings. Anything that comes my way that's hard — as I resist the urge to just run away from everything that's hard, I just ask for blessings, and it helps. The effect is so immediate that it's hard to not believe that it's actually doing something. So it's been very good for my faith and for my reliance on the Buddhas.

The other thing I've been focusing on is what it means to really, purely cherish all other living beings. I started to realize that yes, I want all living beings to be happy, and I can act as if. But some things I'm doing, it's just like, I'm doing it because it's the right thing to do. And when I ask myself, do you really care whether or not all other living beings are happy? To be honest, the answer is no. I'm doing it, I want them to be happy, but that's very different from caring.

practiceReports.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceReports.text:
Thanks, Fran. Fantastic. So yeah, keeping that blessing channel open. Sometimes it takes a bit to get the familiarity going, to really ask for blessings and feel those blessings. But once we have the channel open through familiarity and the karma has been created, then it's just like turning a tap. And they flow. Don't turn it off. Ever. Just let it flow.

And yeah, good point about cherishing others. There's so much that we do because it's quote-unquote the right thing to do. But cherishing others has nothing to do with our external behavior. It's simply a mind — the thought: you are important, and your happiness and freedom are important. So external behavior has zero percent to do with it. Not one percent, not eighteen percent. Zero percent. Because cherishing others is a mind.

practiceReports.speaker: Anne K
practiceReports.text:
My mind has gotten a little noisier again. I was trying very hard to just not think. That doesn't really work super good. And I realized what I had forgotten is the reason I'm thinking too much is because I'm trying to solve problems. So I just made it a habit again to whenever I have a problem, just give it to my spiritual guide. Be like, I can't figure this out, you do it.

And when I give it to the Buddhas, I'm like, they're working on it at some level. And it frees me to just focus on what's in front of me. And it really works. My mind has been a lot more spacious again since I started to do that.

practiceReports.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceReports.text: Yeah, that's nice. Just bring in the Buddhas to help solve the problems. Do you think your mind's more busy because of the job? Yeah — that's also a good data point. What are the conditions where our mind goes up and what are the conditions where our mind goes down? It's a great teaching. What are the tools I need to navigate them?

practiceReports.speaker: Mary Ann
practiceReports.text:
I was trying to make a decision from a place of anxiety and fear. So that would not be a good place to make decisions. Somehow it became evident that I should practice affectionate love. I did a lot of it, most of it on the subway, just sort of imagining introducing myself to each person and saying, I don't know you, but I think you could just be great if I wasn't fearful and it was peaceful.

And then one day I was like, oh my God, I have so many friends. This is amazing. And that made me feel a lot less fearful of other people, which I think was really getting in my way of affectionate love. When I just thought about their inner self, I was like, what am I afraid of?

practiceReports.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceReports.text:
Thanks, Mary Ann. Two points there. One is just try not to solve our problems from an unpeaceful place. When we're really busy and start to feel unpeaceful, we think it's because of all these problems. So I just need to get the problems out of the way and then I'll be peaceful again. But the way we're trying to solve the problems is with the unpeaceful mind. It's actually the cause of all the problems.

And yeah, affectionate love — that was the little magic pill for a peaceful mind. It's definitely one of the easiest virtuous minds to get to that brings peace. Really worth its weight in gold.

practiceReports.speaker: Mimi
practiceReports.text:
Two weeks ago, I took as one of the sixteen conceptual thoughts the one being that samsara is suffering. And so for two weeks, I have not done that at all. Because things have been going great these past two weeks. Juliana went to her prom, and she got an award, and she's graduating, and everything is so happy. But it's a good reminder.

Because I'm like, you're definitely going for refuge and really asking the Buddhas when things are going really bad and you're really suffering. But here I am, floating around, and I'm not thinking that samsara is in the nature of suffering. So I was like, okay, what are you going to do? And I thought, well, I'm going to just do taking of my future suffering. I'm just going to remind myself that it's coming. Aging, sickness — it's going to come. So better prepare.

practiceReports.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceReports.text:
Yeah, thanks, Mimi. The main thing there is when we have a meditation break practice, it's the checking in that gives us wisdom. It didn't happen — which is actually fine. But what's not fine is when we don't check in and establish the lesson from that. Because then we're just cheating ourselves, setting up these little determinations that we never check in about. And then they don't happen. And we don't care. And we create this inauthenticity in our own wishes.

So one insight was: I can be a bit of a fair-weather Dharma practitioner. Things are good — eh, I don't need any of that. Oh, fantastic insight. How can I use that next time? Those insights are huge. They're going to change our life if we really get the lesson.

Every try in any kind of practice — it really doesn't matter how it goes. It's what we learn from it. One moment of a disappointing shot doesn't change the scale at all. The lessons we get can change the scale massively. We only get those lessons if we check in and establish a conclusion.

practiceReports.speaker: Anne P
practiceReports.text: My spiritual practice has been working on non-virtuous states of mind. And lately, I identified a big one — it was my sister. I blame my sister for letting her dementia get worse. So I'm meditating about it, thinking, I remember, roll all blame into one. And in my meditation, it came to me that if my real striving is to love people, and every time I'm having negative thoughts and treating my sister poorly, that's like putting a big boulder in my path. Here I am trying to go down this path where I'm loving more people, and every negative thought about people, particularly my sister or loved ones, is making it harder and harder.

practiceReports.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceReports.text:
Yeah, thank you. Nice insight. We're trying to love all living beings, but often these people who are really close to us, we kind of don't love particularly. And somehow they get left out. Loving all living beings was too abstract, too general — it wasn't really true, because they're in all living beings.

The point is taking those close relationships and thinking these are our little trainers. These are the people we're really practicing with. Our spouse, our kids, our parents, our siblings, our close friends, our neighbors, our close co-workers. That's where our practice is happening.

practiceReports.speaker: Jose
practiceReports.text:
A few bits and pieces from the last three or four classes. First, on frustration and respect — since we studied that, I found a way to use it in my practice of cherishing others. Applying the mind of respect to strangers is way easier for me than feeling that I cherish them. Maybe I don't think you're the most important person in the world, but I can definitely respect you, and if I deeply respect you, then I feel like that's taking me in the right direction.

Second, since I came back from the festival, I took on the practice of water bowl offerings. That's been beautiful. It's a floor practice that leads into seven limb prayers, and I can feel the seven limbs more deeply now.

Finally, I've been pondering how going for refuge ultimately means going for refuge to emptiness. There's a passage in the Request to the Lord of All Lineages in the refuge part that says, by engaging this mind continuously, I will attain the actual refuge in my mind. I never really thought about what those sentences meant, but now it's super obvious — it is emptiness in the end.

practiceReports.speaker: Ryan
practiceReports.text:
I want to follow up on the water bowls. I had this shrine set up in my home with nice water bowls. For months, they sat there and I ignored them. I'd find all excuses. I would rather sit down and do the hard meditation than pour the water off. Until KK was sharing the teachings about finding the light in it. I said, okay, maybe I can't find the light, but at least it will help me with my miserliness.

So I started doing offerings about four to five days a week. And one day, about a week ago, I noticed I was smiling while doing it. I was gladly sharing the water. I was like, hmm, this is not Ryan. Something's off with me.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: MTB paragraphs 340–344: Confession of Non-Virtue and the Four Opponent Powers
teaching.text:
Okay, so Geshe-la says here, page 84: “The three limbs of offering, prostration, and refuge are the preliminary practices leading up to the main practice described in this chapter — the confession of non-virtue.”

That's really interesting. Even refuge is still a preliminary for this practice. It's showing that confession is the main deal, the main course. It's a complete total practice. All Dharma is within confession.

“This confession or declaration of our non-virtuous actions enables us to counteract the harmful effects these actions would otherwise bring upon us. The full and proper completion of this practice depends upon utilizing the four opponent powers listed below. If these four powers are completed properly with full understanding of their meaning, all our past non-virtue can definitely be purified.”

We're going to be doing this chapter for all of June. Maybe we can all think of June as a little purification retreat. Even if we can't be here, even if we have other things going on, we can still think: this is my purification retreat.

Let's fall in love with confession and purification. The four powers — regret, reliance, the opponent force, the power of the promise — we study them sequentially, but really it's one practice with four parts. Like a concerto. They're not isolated, siloed practices. And if you get stuck on one, it's probably because you're relating to it in a disconnected way. Put it in context with the other three, and it will flow.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: MTB paragraphs 345+: The Power of Regret
teaching.text:
“The first step in purifying the effects of negative actions is to admit to ourselves that they were indeed negative and harmful. This sincere admission of the wrongs we have done, both to ourselves and others, allows the process of uprooting these negativities to begin.”

These two points are very rich. Is there something in us that doesn't want to admit that? What's that about? Who are we hiding it from? It's just ourselves. What's the mechanism inside our heart when we're not admitting?

And ‘the wrongs we have done, both to ourselves and others.’ I love that. The delusions do wrongs to us. We're purifying the harm that's been done to ourselves through the delusions.

Elsewhere, Geshe-la said that the Tibetan word for confession means to crack open a rotten log and reveal it to the sun. When we're not wanting to admit it, we're trying to protect the self we normally see — our samsara. When we just open it up, the rotten log has no power to protect itself anymore. It gets exposed to the sun, and the rot starts to evaporate. Buddha's love is like warm, healing rays on it. But if we close it and hide it, it just festers.

Part of the reason we don't admit is psychological defenses. Part is because we don't know how to purify. Part is because we're blaming ourselves and not the delusions. And part is simply that we don't remember — we have negativities from past lives that we can't recall. The confession verses that follow are a practice that helps melt the veneer blocking those memories. Read them once a day if you can.

“With a deep sense of regret for my past non-virtues, I press my palms together, beseeching those who possess great compassion, all the Buddhas and superior bodhisattvas abiding in the ten directions. From beginningless time in this and in previous lives, having been ignorant of the law of actions and their effects, I have personally committed much non-virtue, and have also impelled others to do so. Overwhelmed by deceptive ignorance, I have even rejoiced in the non-virtue others have performed. But now I recognize all these actions as mistakes, and from the depths of my heart, I sincerely declare them all in your presence, O protectors.”

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Four characteristics of karma applied to negative karma
teaching.text:
“Now, if I die without cleansing myself of these great evils, I will undoubtedly come to experience unimaginable suffering.”

There's nothing more essential to get in the whole practice of purification. That's the thesis. If I die without purifying my mind, I will undoubtedly come to experience unimaginable suffering. Undoubtedly.

Do I believe that? Sometimes we'll find: somewhat no. My faith and understanding of karma is a little weak. So it's an invitation — how can I upgrade my karma understanding?

The four general characteristics of karma help. The results of actions are definite: negative karma will 100% lead to suffering if not purified. The results of actions increase: until it's purified, it's growing, spreading into other crevices of our mind, getting more powerful every day. If an action is not performed, its results cannot be experienced — practically, when negative karma ripens, instead of thinking ‘it shouldn't have happened,’ we think: I didn't create the karma for it to turn out differently. An action is never wasted: time doesn't make it go away, death doesn't make it go away, just being a nice person doesn't make it go away. There are only two ways it goes away: purification or experiencing the suffering.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: Queen Noh Sangma story and the core insight
teaching.text:
In the scriptures, the example is given of Queen Noh Sangma, who followed a Buddhist teacher and gained the realization of a never-returner. She gathered a following of 500 female disciples who all developed miracle powers. One day, the building in which they were assembled caught fire. The queen and all her disciples immediately flew into the sky, but the queen understood that they had all created the collective karma to die in the fire that day. Since this karma was already ripening, it was unavoidable. She said: the only way we can now purify our non-virtuous actions is by experiencing the effect. All the women flew back into the fire, like moths leaping into a candle flame.

The women had a poor maidservant called Gertchog — gotta love Gertchog — who had no miracle powers and had to escape by running through the sewers. She alone escaped, because she alone had not created the karma to die in that fire.

Please just come back to that one point. If you get distracted or confused or whatever, it all hinges on this: negative karma that's not purified equals unavoidable suffering. It's guaranteed. Chisel it into our mental DNA.

teaching.speaker: Ben
teaching.text: Something that's always confused me — it's described as this karmic potential is created and then causes and conditions come together that make it ripen. But how do you know which things to categorize as causes and conditions? Presumably, those are also results of karma. What really causes my mind to escape into laziness is not that I'll manipulate the conditions — I just might happen to get lucky and get away with it.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
Yeah, we might get lucky and get away with it. This is the kind of thing where we have to spend time in incredible pain and suffering more often. Go find people who are dying. Go to an Alzheimer's ward. Spend time with those people.

The conditions we're in now — bubble Brooklyn, with our Dharma practice — is like 0.0001% of samsara in comfort. Once you move even to the 99th percentile, the top 1% of samsara, we're already in absolute abject agony. Profound mental torment and pain.

This feeling like I can get away with it is because we have a data set of a lot of people getting somewhat lucky right now. We need to expose our mind more to suffering. I have a very dear person in my life who every time I talk to them, they're telling me about some genocide going on in the world that I don't know about yet. They're not getting angry or worldly about it. They're just trying to expose their mind constantly to suffering to develop compassion, to counterbalance the bubble world we're in.

No one gets lucky in samsara. Not one person in the long run.

teaching.speaker: Ryan
teaching.text: You said we should think of it as a purification month. And now everything, if it's not purified, it's going to lead to unimaginable suffering. Since some of us are doing the Lamrim throughout the month every day, how can we tie this purification month together with the Lamrim?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
Good point. We don't want to silo them and think about them as separate. Every time we do our Lamrim practice, it's a purification practice. It's definitely the opponent force. But also, compassion is the most powerful purifying force in the universe. When we do the refuge meditation in Lamrim, that's reliance. When we're thinking about death, that's increasing our regret. All the love-based meditations are part of reliance, the bodhichitta part of it.

So it's all just one practice. Having a purification month and meditating on Lamrim all month — they're not two things. It's one thing.

dedication.speaker: Kadam Kyle
dedication.text: Main point: if our negative karma is not purified, it will definitely lead to unavoidable suffering. That's what we want to get completely crystal clear in our heart. Everything else will flow from there. Let's take a break now. We'll come back at 6:15. We can dedicate. Through the virtues we've collected, through practicing, meditating, discussing — may all living beings find lasting peace of mind, enlightenment.

chantedPrayers.text: Liberating Prayer O Blessed One, Shakyamuni Buddha, precious Treasury of Compassion, Bestower of Supreme Inner Peace. You who love all beings without exception are the source of happiness and goodness, and you guide us to the liberating path. Your body is a wish-fulfilling jewel, your speech is supreme, purifying nectar, and your mind is refuge for all living beings. With folded palms I turn to you, Supreme unchanging Friend. I request from the depths of my heart, please give me the light of your wisdom to dispel the darkness of my mind and to heal my mental continuum. Please nourish me with your goodness, that I in turn may nourish all beings with an unceasing banquet of delight. Through your compassionate intention, your blessings and virtuous deeds, and my strong wish to rely upon you, may all suffering quickly cease and all happiness and joy be fulfilled, and may holy Dharma flourish forevermore.

announcements.speaker: Kadam Kyle
announcements.text:
A couple of announcements. This coming Thursday, we have Offering to the Spiritual Guide, also called Dharma Chakra Day — turning the wheel of Dharma Day. It's also Geshe-la's birthday, so we celebrate both. There'll be a little teaching from 7 to 7:15, then we'll go into the practice until about 9. That's the 4th.

Then the 6th, we have our day course: Creating a Win-Win World. And then on the 11th, we have a free public talk at the Bed-Stuy branch on healing our body and mind through meditation. We're bringing our whole FP squad there that day, so we won't have class in person on Thursday here — we're all going to Bed-Stuy to support the branch.

When we think about the branches at the center, we never think about them as separate. They're future centers. It's like branching off the main center, but then those branches become their own little hubs and branch off into their areas. And then we can benefit the whole world through this network.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: MTB continued: death, impermanence, and the impersonal nature of death
teaching.text:
Back to purification. “I pray to you, please swiftly protect me from all these fears. The duration of my life is totally uncertain, and to the unpredictable Lord of Death, it makes no difference whether I have declared my non-virtues or not. Without waiting for me to complete the work I am engaged in, and unconcerned whether I am sick or healthy, he will suddenly descend upon me.”

Death is completely impersonal. There's no God or whatever rewarding us if we do a good job or punishing us if we do a bad job. There's no mercy involved. There's no volition in the law of karma. It's an impersonal force. There's no arc or story that our life is following. We're simply alive because our karma right now is not ripening in the form of death. And then it will change and we'll just die.

Nagarjuna said: we maintain our life in the midst of thousands of conditions that threaten death. Our life force abides like a candle flame in the breeze. It is possible to die an untimely death even before completing our lifespan, because we can exhaust our merit sooner than we exhaust the karma that determines lifespan.

I find it very helpful to meditate on the point: this dream may end today. When a dream ends, how much warning do you get? It just ends. You shift to another realm, another reality. Our death is like that.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.note: MTB continued: confession verses and imagining death without purification
teaching.text:
“During my life, I did not understand that my relatives, my body, wealth, possessions, and everything would all be left behind, and that I would depart alone from this life for the next. Out of my ignorance, I committed much non-virtue for the sake of my relatives and friends, and did much evil trying to destroy my foes. Now I see the foolishness of such actions, and I deeply regret my past deeds.”

We've done this billions and billions of times. In each life, if our ignorance is functioning, we make it all about that life and those people, as if the stakes are unimaginably high. We end up creating a lot of non-virtue to protect them and go against people we don't like. And then it all disappears. How many times have we said, ‘We'll be together forever’? Billions of times. And then we die. We forget about them. And now we're mating with a cockroach.

“With my non-virtues still undeclared and the practice of Dharma ignored, the Lord of Death will suddenly swoop down. While lying upon my deathbed, though surrounded by a circle of friends and relatives, I alone will experience intense suffering and fear as my life is severed. Seized by the frightening messengers of the Lord of Death, of what benefit are these relatives and friends? Completely helpless, my desolation will be extreme. With large, gaping eyes, I will look in the four directions for someone to give me refuge. But seeing no source of refuge anywhere, I will become completely enshrouded in gloom and despair.”

These verses are designed to lead to wisdom fear — a peaceful, virtuous mind. The key is identifying: the entirety of these effects comes from karma that can be purified. When we think bad things come from the outside, we think we can build outer security. But once we start thinking this is entirely from within — entirely mental projections — it ups the wisdom fear a lot. There's zero outer security we can set up. But it also ratchets up the answer: all we have to do is purify the mind.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
So to sum up: point one, we want to admit the negativity in our mind — stop the denial, crack open the rotten log. Point two, all the negativity, if not purified, will definitely lead to suffering. Point three, we looked at the biases and unconscious blockers — feeling like we're on an arc, that death won't come, that we're a good Buddhist. We oppose that by thinking: my life is like a candle flame about to die in the wind. This dream may end today. And lastly, we tried to imagine what it's like to actually die without having purified that negative karma. Making it visceral and alive so the wisdom fear gets stoked.

Any ponderings before discussion?

teaching.speaker: Anne K
teaching.text: I've often wondered why purification isn't all our main practice all the time. Because to me, it's the one that makes the most sense. I've personally gotten the most bang for the buck from it. But we're told, no, we should be doing Heart Jewel and Lamrim. Maybe my problem is not thinking carefully enough about how those practices are purification practices.

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
They are purification practices, definitely. The everything that we need is three things: accumulating merit, purifying negativity, and receiving blessings. Purification removes all the obstacles. But it doesn't create all the merit that we need to attain enlightenment. It's just clearing away obstacles.

Purification is like getting rid of the obstacles. Merit is like creating the Buddhahood. And the blessings are the magic that really transforms our mind from Buddha — because our realizations have to come from somewhere.

If someone just did Vajrasattva but ignored Lamrim, they wouldn't create the mindset that prevents new negative karma. They'd keep purifying but never address the root causes. Lamrim gives rise to a lot of that. So purification and Lamrim are not two things — they're one practice.

Sumit — yeah?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
Sumit asks: when I'm experiencing suffering, is that necessarily negative karma ripening? Because I could learn from it, I could have a positive reaction.

Yeah, it's hard to say. If we're really wishing for suffering because we want to practice lojong, and suffering comes, it's like a reward. We're happy about it. Would you call that a negative result? It's hard to say.

The main thing we actually want to purify is the causes of delusions and lower rebirth. Manifest suffering is not as vitally important to purify, because you can transform it. But getting hijacked by delusions or having lower rebirth — those are not easily transformed. That motivates me a lot more than random pain.

David, yeah?

teaching.speaker: David
teaching.text: You just answered one of my questions, which is — it's more important to purify delusions than actual negative actions, maybe? Is that what you were just saying?

teaching.speaker: Kadam Kyle
teaching.text:
Not exactly. What I was saying was: what stokes our real wisdom fear, our wish for purification? Manifest suffering — yeah, but I can also transform that. I'm a lojong practitioner. But delusions and lower rebirth, and just generally samsaric rebirth — that's a lot more motivating, because there's not really a transforming that can happen there. If delusions hijack us for the rest of this life, it's too late.

Okay, let's have time for discussion now. David, do you have some partners?

teaching.speaker: David
teaching.text: Jose and Neil, David and Sumit, Byron and Brian, Fran and Mary Ann, Anne K and Mimi, Anne P and Suzanne.

pairedDiscussion.note: Paired discussion removed. Audio heavily garbled in both Whale and Dolphin. Separate trio of Kristin, Grady, and Ben self-organized.

conclusion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
conclusion.text: Alright, does anyone have anything they'd like to share or declare? Something about purification that we should do over the week? David, yeah.

conclusion.speaker: David
conclusion.text: Just bringing in an intention to purify — bringing a purification intention into all of our Dharma activities, viewing it as an opponent force.

conclusion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
conclusion.text: Yeah, that's a great idea. It's just like a little muscle. We can make everything a purification if we have that intention. Anything we do. Fran — did you have something?

conclusion.speaker: Anne K
conclusion.text: I like the idea — when we have these sort of anxieties about minor everyday things, to remember what we really should be worried about is that we are definitely going to be reborn in the lower realms. That'll put things in perspective.

conclusion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
conclusion.text: Yeah, all the little paper cuts of life — they all fade away once you think about the big picture of samsara and the huge machine that it is. Trillions of migrating beings moving from one realm to the other. Billions and billions of lives that we've had. The little paper cuts of life just seem like nothing. They don't like me — it doesn't matter at all. All this little drama at work — it's really nothing actually. I'm going to put my mind on something bigger. Yeah, it's very helpful to move our mind to a mind of purification when we encounter those little instances.

conclusion.speaker: Fran
conclusion.text: I was very moved by the phrase about the harm that we do to ourselves and others — that we do to ourselves. If I'm feeling a certain way that's negative, it's because I've created the karma for myself to feel that way. Besides that I probably made somebody else feel like that, and now by buying into it, I'm just recreating that negative karma and tendency over and over and over again. I never thought about it before as something — I always thought about it as having that tendency because I made somebody else feel like that. Not because I did that to myself as well.

conclusion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
conclusion.text: Yeah, bringing in the harm that we've done to ourselves as a deepening of our understanding of karma and purification. Anything else? Oh, Kristin slash Grady?

conclusion.speaker: Kristin
conclusion.text: We were talking with Ben about this idea that if we die without purifying, we're definitely going to experience these sufferings that are all projections from our own mind. And Ben was saying all the suffering he has seen, he knows he would experience because it's come from his mind — it's in there to be experienced.

conclusion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
conclusion.text: Yeah, that's super helpful. When we try to ignore the suffering in the world, it's really pointless — because it's all coming from our mind. All the suffering in the world is showing us what's in our own mind. All the atrocities — they're all coming from within our mind. Those beings are just imputed as other out of ignorance. They're appearances to the mind. We can't ignore that and run away from it. It's showing us our own karma. If my mind can appear that throughout this world, then that's inside me.

dedication.speaker: Kadam Kyle
dedication.text: Okay, we can dedicate now. We can think through the virtues we've collected, through practicing, meditating, discussing. May all living beings find lasting peace of mind, enlightenment. You can make any personal prayers or dedications. Okay, thank you. Thanks, everyone. It was a delight.
